The **2011–12 Harvard Crimson men's basketball team** was one of the most successful in program history, marking a turning point for Harvard basketball under head coach **Tommy Amaker**. The team achieved several historic milestones, including its first **Ivy League championship** in 66 years (since 1946) and its first **NCAA Tournament appearance** since 1946. Here’s a detailed breakdown of the season:

---

### **Key Details**
- **Head Coach**: Tommy Amaker (6th season at Harvard)
- **Record**: 26–5 (12–2 Ivy League)
- **Conference Finish**: 1st (Ivy League Champions)
- **Postseason**:
  - **NCAA Tournament**: Lost to **Vanderbilt** (79–70) in the **Round of 64** (as a **#12 seed** in the East Region).
  - **NIT**: Did not participate (automatic NCAA bid via Ivy League title).
- **Final Rankings**:
  - **AP Poll**: Received votes (not ranked in Top 25).
  - **Coaches Poll**: Received votes.
  - **KenPom Ranking**: #53 (highest in Ivy League history at the time).

---

### **Roster & Key Players**
The team was led by a mix of experienced upperclassmen and talented underclassmen, with a strong emphasis on **defense, three-point shooting, and ball movement**.

#### **Starters & Key Contributors**:
1. **Keith Wright (Sr., C, 6'8")**
   - **Stats**: 10.8 PPG, 8.5 RPG, 1.3 BPG
   - **Accolades**: **Ivy League Player of the Year**, 1st Team All-Ivy
   - **Role**: Dominant low-post presence, defensive anchor, and leader.

2. **Brandyn Curry (Jr., G, 6'1")**
   - **Stats**: 9.7 PPG, 5.1 APG, 1.8 SPG
   - **Accolades**: 1st Team All-Ivy
   - **Role**: Floor general, elite passer, and perimeter defender.

3. **Laurent Rivard (So., G, 6'5")**
   - **Stats**: 10.0 PPG, 43.6% 3PT
   - **Role**: Sharpshooter (set Harvard’s single-season 3PT record with **88 makes**).

4. **Christian Webster (Jr., G, 6'5")**
   - **Stats**: 10.0 PPG, 3.5 RPG
   - **Role**: Versatile wing, clutch scorer.

5. **Oliver McNally (Sr., G, 6'3")**
   - **Stats**: 8.4 PPG, 3.9 APG
   - **Role**: Veteran leader, steady guard play.

#### **Key Bench Players**:
- **Kyle Casey (Jr., F, 6'7")** – 10.0 PPG, 5.5 RPG (injured late in the season but critical early on).
- **Wes Saunders (Fr., G, 6'5")** – 3.8 PPG (future Ivy League Player of the Year).
- **Steve Moundou-Missi (Fr., F, 6'7")** – 2.5 PPG (emerged as a key player in later years).

---

### **Season Highlights**
#### **Non-Conference Success**
- **7–1 start**, including wins over **Florida State (46–41)** and **Central Florida (72–62)**.
- **Lost to UConn (67–53)** in the **Battle 4 Atlantis** (Huskies were defending national champs).
- **Defeated Boston College (71–69)** – First win over an ACC team since 2009.

#### **Ivy League Dominance**
- **12–2 record**, clinching the **Ivy League title outright** (first since 1946).
- **Key Wins**:
  - **Harvard 56, Princeton 50** (Feb. 11, 2012) – Clinched a share of the Ivy title.
  - **Harvard 70, Penn 58** (March 6, 2012) – Secured the outright championship.
- **Only losses**: At Princeton (70–62) and at Penn (55–54).

#### **NCAA Tournament Appearance**
- **#12 seed** in the **East Region**, facing **#5 Vanderbilt** (SEC).
- **Game Recap (March 16, 2012)**:
  - Harvard led **67–66** with under 5 minutes left but fell **79–70**.
  - **Keith Wright** (13 pts, 8 reb), **Laurent Rivard** (20 pts, 6–9 3PT).
  - Vanderbilt’s **John Jenkins** (27 pts) and **Festus Ezeli** (17 pts, 8 reb) proved too much.
- **Significance**: First NCAA Tournament game for Harvard since **1946** (lost to Ohio State in the Elite Eight that year).

---

### **Historical Significance**
1. **First Ivy League Title in 66 Years**:
   - Ended a drought dating back to **1946** (when Harvard shared the title with Yale).
   - First **outright** Ivy championship since **1936**.

2. **First NCAA Tournament Bid Since 1946**:
   - Harvard had **never won an NCAA Tournament game** (still true as of 2024).
   - The 2012 appearance began a **string of 4 straight NCAA Tournaments** (2012–2015) under Amaker.

3. **Rise of Harvard Basketball**:
   - Proved Harvard could compete nationally, leading to **future NBA players** (Jeremy Lin’s brother **Joseph Lin** was a walk-on, but later players like **Wes Saunders** and **Siyani Chambers** emerged).
   - **Tommy Amaker** became the **winningest coach in Harvard history** (209–106 at Harvard as of 2024).

4. **Academic & Athletic Balance**:
   - The team had a **3.0+ cumulative GPA**, embodying the "student-athlete" ideal.

---

### **Aftermath & Legacy**
- **2012–13 Season**: Harvard **repeated as Ivy champs**, earned a **#14 seed**, and **upset #3 New Mexico** in the NCAA Tournament (first tourney win in school history).
- **Key Players’ Futures**:
  - **Keith Wright**: Played professionally in Europe (Germany, France).
  - **Brandyn Curry**: Left Harvard after the **2012–13 academic scandal** (withdrew for a year, later played at **LIU Brooklyn**).
  - **Laurent Rivard**: Became Harvard’s **all-time leader in three-pointers** (240).
  - **Wes Saunders**: **2015 Ivy League Player of the Year**, played in the **NBA G League**.
- **Tommy Amaker**: Left Harvard in **2022** to become **head coach at Seton Hall**.

---

### **Fun Facts & Trivia**
- **Harvard’s "Three-Headed Monster"**: Rivard, Webster, and Curry combined for **230 three-pointers** (a school record at the time).
- **Defensive Prowess**: Harvard allowed **just 58.9 PPG** (11th in the nation).
- **Ivy League Attendance Boom**: Home games at **Lavietes Pavilion** saw record crowds (capacity: 2,195).
- **Jeremy Lin Connection**: Though **Jeremy Lin** (Harvard ’10) had already graduated, his **2012 "Linsanity"** with the Knicks brought extra attention to Harvard hoops.

---

### **Final Thoughts**
The **2011–12 Harvard Crimson** were **trailblazers**, shattering the perception that Ivy League teams couldn’t compete at a high level. Their success **elevated the program** to new heights, leading to **multiple NCAA Tournament appearances** and **NBA attention** for future players. While they didn’t win a tournament game, their **Ivy League title and NCAA berth** were **monumental achievements** that changed Harvard basketball forever.
